cells.title: Source
body: The Colorado Court of Appeals published Al-Hamim v. Star Hearthstone, LLC, 2024COA128, on December 26, 2024.
The opinion addressed an appeal by a self-represented litigant whose opening brief contained citations the court could not locate.

cells.title: Observed behavior
body: The appellant confirmed that citations in the opening brief were hallucinations produced after relying on AI to assist with preparation.
The court affirmed the judgment and declined to sanction the appellant in that case, while giving notice that future filings containing GAI-produced hallucinations may result in sanctions.

cells.source: Al-Hamim v. Star Hearthstone, LLC, paragraph 25
cells.label: Fake citations listed by the court

examples: L&M Inv. Co. v. Morrison, 469 P.2d 516 (Colo. App. 1970)

cells.source: Al-Hamim v. Star Hearthstone, LLC, paragraph 26
cells.output: The court recorded that Al-Hamim admitted relying on AI to assist preparation, confirmed the citations were hallucinations, and said he failed to inspect the brief.

The file uses the opinion for the citations, the appellant's response, and the court's disposition.

cells.title: Notes
body: The opinion did not identify the AI tool.
This file is separate from Mata v. Avianca because the primary artifact is a different court record and involves a self-represented litigant.
